# Aakash Dhar
> Technical Project Manager. 8.5 years as a backend developer, now running client delivery at BetaCraft across enterprise integration (CRM, ERP, APIs) and AI systems in production. Open to senior technical delivery roles in Europe.

Aakash Dhar is a Technical Project Manager and former backend developer who builds the AI tooling his delivery teams run on. This site is his portfolio: case studies of real client delivery, and essays on project management, agentic AI, and how the PM role is changing.

## Key pages
- [Aakash Dhar · Technical Project Manager · AI & Integration](https://aakashdhar.me/): Aakash Dhar — Technical Project Manager with 8.5 years as a backend developer. Enterprise integration (CRM, ERP, APIs) and AI systems in production at BetaCraft. Open to senior delivery roles in Europe.
- [Now](https://aakashdhar.me/now.html): What Aakash Dhar is focused on right now: EU AI governance, planning a move to the Netherlands, and shipping AI systems at BetaCraft.

## Case studies
- [Brieflex · Case Study](https://aakashdhar.me/case-studies/case-study-brieflex.html): Brieflex was an AI-powered California Bar Exam training platform with a live client and no sprint structure. I audited the project, reset the delivery process, and drove it toward commercial launch.
- [Link Broadband · Case Study](https://aakashdhar.me/case-studies/case-study-link-broadband.html): A marketing website, a HubSpot lifecycle automation layer, and a clean handoff into third-party checkout: built, integrated, and launched in four weeks. The real job was defining exactly what each system owned.
- [PM–Dev Closed Loop · Case Study](https://aakashdhar.me/case-studies/case-study-pm-dev-loop.html): BetaCraft's end-to-end AI-native delivery system: a 28-skill pipeline where a client email enters one end and a tested, reviewed, client-ready delivery exits the other, without the PM seeing code or the developer seeing a client message.
- [Promptly · Case Study](https://aakashdhar.me/case-studies/case-study-promptly.html): Promptly is a macOS app that converts voice into structured AI prompts. I built it for myself: a case study on building with no client brief, no scope negotiation, and every bad product decision shipping into your own workflow.
- [Regulatory Compliance Platform · Case Study](https://aakashdhar.me/case-studies/case-study-sapey.html): How I stepped into a stalled US regulatory compliance platform where three organisations disagreed on what was built: ran the production API tests, surfaced six SOW discrepancies, and rebuilt the factual record so delivery could move on evidence.
- [TokoSmart · Case Study](https://aakashdhar.me/case-studies/case-study-tokosmart.html): TokoSmart was a World Bank-commissioned research app for Indonesian warung owners on a fixed institutional deadline. A compliance gap and a blocked distribution channel surfaced mid-sprint with 400 participants waiting, both resolved inside the sprint.

## Writing
- [What Should a PM Learn Now That the Busywork Is Gone?](https://aakashdhar.me/blog/what-should-a-pm-learn-now-that-the-busywork-is-gone.html): When the admin a PM got good at becomes free, the skills left standing are all judgment, not production. The bet worth making now is getting better at being right.
- [When AI Does the Satisfying Part, What's Left to Enjoy?](https://aakashdhar.me/blog/when-ai-does-the-satisfying-part-whats-left-to-enjoy.html): AI can make a team faster and, in the same motion, remove the craft that made the work feel good. Satisfaction is load-bearing, and protecting it is quietly part of the job now.
- [The Technical Debt You Can't See in a Fast Team](https://aakashdhar.me/blog/the-technical-debt-you-cant-see-in-a-fast-team.html): A fast AI-assisted team leaves a new kind of debt: not one big shortcut, but a thousand small defaults nobody remembers choosing. The PM has to go looking while the chart is green.
- [You Can't Plan a Quarter When the Tools Change Every Month](https://aakashdhar.me/blog/you-cant-plan-a-quarter-when-the-tools-change-every-month.html): When AI capability shifts every few weeks, a detailed quarterly plan becomes a confident bet on a world you can no longer see. Plan the direction firmly and the route loosely.
- [What Are Clients Paying For When They Can Watch the AI Work?](https://aakashdhar.me/blog/what-are-clients-paying-for-when-they-can-watch-the-ai-work.html): When a client can watch AI build in an hour, effort stops justifying the invoice. What they are really paying for is judgment, and you had better be able to name it.
- [When Building Is Cheap, Saying "Not Yet" Gets Expensive](https://aakashdhar.me/blog/when-building-is-cheap-saying-not-yet-gets-expensive.html): When AI makes building nearly free, the cost that used to filter out bad ideas disappears. The PM's leverage moves to the front of the pipeline: guarding what gets started.
- [Who Trains the Junior When the Agent Does the Grunt Work?](https://aakashdhar.me/blog/who-trains-the-junior-when-the-agent-does-the-grunt-work.html): Juniors used to build judgment by doing the boring work. AI does that work in seconds now, so teaching a beginner has to become deliberate, not a side effect.

- [What Happens to the PM When the Team Ships Twice as Fast](https://aakashdhar.me/blog/pm-when-the-team-ships-faster.html): When AI doubles a team's output, the intuition is that the PM gets breathing room. Instead the bottleneck moves to the part of delivery that never speeds up:
